description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order.
intuition: Since the input is sorted, the largest squares come from either end (large negative or large positive numbers). Use two pointers from both ends, comparing absolute values and filling the result array from the largest position backward.
approach: Use two pointers at the start and end. The largest square is either from the most negative or most positive value. Build the result array from right to left.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: nums = [-4,-1,0,3,10]
n=5, left=0, right=4. Fill result from position 4 down to 0.
i=4: abs(-4)=4 vs abs(10)=10. 4 < 10 → result[4]=100, right=3.
i=3: abs(-4)=4 vs abs(3)=3. 4 > 3 → result[3]=16, left=1.
i=2: abs(-1)=1 vs abs(3)=3. 1 < 3 → result[2]=9, right=2.
i=1: abs(-1)=1 vs abs(0)=0. 1 > 0 → result[1]=1, left=2.
i=0: left==right==2, abs(0)=0 vs abs(0)=0 → result[0]=0, right=1.
Result: [0,1,9,16,100]
explanation:
1. Two pointers: l at the start, r at the end.
2. Compare absolute values at both pointers.
3. Place the larger square at the current position (filling right to left).
4. Move the pointer that was used.
5. This gives a sorted result in O(n) time.
hints: The largest squared values come from the extremes of the array.
Use two pointers from both ends, filling the result from the back.
Compare absolute values to decide which pointer to use.
